verified_rules.fact: AbilityStandard CastToTarget/Directly/InputPosition receive the Boolean firstAttack. Their ordinary C# branches pass it to set_firstAttack; the backing byte is offset 0x114. The property can also be replaced by a hotfix delegate.

Character.States.AttackState.OnEnter invokes _StartAttack(true) after its entry guards; _NextAttackOrExit invokes _StartAttack(false) after target search. _StartAttack forwards the same Boolean to slot 33 CastToTarget through helper 0x180012f30. This distinguishes entry and continuation of that native state, not first use in a deployment or first use of each animation candidate.

AbilityRandomGroup.CastToTarget preserves the caller Boolean and passes it to the selected child through slot 33. CastDirectly also forwards its supplied Boolean through slot 34. Changing from A to B or C does not itself set firstAttack true.

AttackState finish callback sets m_nextEscapeTime = fixedPlayTime + finishedAbility.escapeTime. It calls _NextAttackOrExit only when this state is still current, reason is not INTERRUPTED (enum 1), and the current attack isReady. The callback timestamp and escapeTime value are not derived here.

If target search or _StartAttack(false) fails, _NextAttackOrExit requests the fallback state only when fixedPlayTime >= m_nextEscapeTime. Before that comparison succeeds it can remain in AttackState, so a target-window gap is not proof of state exit or a fresh firstAttack gate.

AttackState.OnTick checks abnormal-state transition, hasAttack, canUseAtkOrCbt, dialogue-target state, combat switching and current attack readiness. OnExit calls current attack InterruptIfNot; if a distinct raw attack is replaced, it can interrupt that raw attack too, then invokes Unit.OnFinishAttack. These guards are not bound to current calculator movement or interruption windows.
